question:
A randomized controlled trial is conducted to evaluate the relationship between the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan and cardiovascular death in patients with congestive heart failure (diagnosed as ejection fraction < 30%) who are already being treated with an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and a beta blocker. Patients are randomized either to losartan (N = 1500) or placebo (N = 1400). The results of the study show:
Cardiovascular death No cardiovascular death
Losartan + ACE inhibitor + beta blocker 300 1200
Placebo + ACE inhibitor + beta blocker 350 1050
Based on this information, if 200 patients with congestive heart failure and an ejection fraction < 30% were treated with losartan in addition to an ACE inhibitor and a beta blocker, on average, how many cases of cardiovascular death would be prevented?"?
analysis: In this scenario, the absolute risk reduction (ARR) can be calculated by subtracting the event rate in the losartan group from the event rate in the placebo group. ARR = (350/1400) - (300/1500) = 0.05. This means that for every 200 patients treated with losartan, there would be an average reduction of 0.05 cases of cardiovascular death.
